headline: Fed's Waller says AI shopping agents need a new kind of authentication
body: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told Sibos 2026 in Miami on September 29 that agentic commerce changes what payment authentication must prove: not just that a buyer is authorized to pay, but that an agent has authority to pay on the buyer's behalf. He pointed to a possible new payment object, a machine-readable record of delegated authority akin to a digital power of attorney, spelling out what an agent can buy, how much it can spend and when that authority expires.
note: Waller named authentication, liability and fraud as the barriers holding back agent-delegated shopping. Card networks are already filling the gap with their own credentialing schemes, so banks may end up choosing between competing standards before regulators settle on one.
